item.title: Fundamental Physics at the Frontier of Noisy Quantum Computation
item.description:
Pay dirt review — Presents scalable variational algorithms and error-mitigated/error-detected frameworks on up to 120 qubits, giving numerical evidence for inelastic particle production in scalar field theory and exceeding unencoded local observable estimation by >200% at late times using [[4,2,2]] encoded circuits in 2D Ising simulations.

Grade 0.474 · 3.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Practical quantum advantage in quantum simulation” · Nikita A. Zemlevskiy

Asks

How can quantum simulation algorithms, error management strategies, and quantum-information tools be co-designed to simulate fundamental quantum field theory dynamics and scattering processes on noisy-to-partially-fault-tolerant quantum processors?

But

Ancilla leakage and lack of fast resets cause effective inter-block coupling slowdown Jeff=J(1−2pflip); higher syndrome measurement rounds inject coherence-time noise that can outweigh error detection.

Tools

SC-ADAPT-VQE · Scalable Variational Circuits (SVC) · [[4,2,2]] quantum error-detecting code · IBM superconducting quantum processors · Matrix Product State (MPS) simulations

Abstract

Quantum computing offers a new, orthogonal direction for investigating fundamental physics, extending beyond classical numerical methods and conventional observables. Realizing this potential requires directly confronting the noise limiting currently available quantum computers. Progress rests on advancing algorithms, interpreting their results, and managing their errors together. This thesis presents several advancements in the use of quantum simulation and quantum information to probe fundamental physics. The first is in the use of quantum computers to simulate collisions in quantum field theories. Central to these simulations are new wavepacket preparation, time evolution, and error mitigation techniques, which allow for simulations with some of the largest effective circuit volumes to date. These methods enable the first quantum simulation providing numerical evidence for inelastic particle production, a key process in fundamental physics. The second advancement centers on the role quantum-information-theoretic quantities play in physical processes. Beyond mere correlations with the physics of the process, entanglement and magic are shown to probe the interactions present in scattering and hadronization dynamics. A precision study requires a complete quantification of algorithmic and hardware uncertainties, an outstanding goal as quantum simulations mature. The third advancement in this thesis addresses error management. A framework minimizing the effect of algorithmic errors in analog quantum simulations is presented. In a step toward fault tolerance, error detection in encoded quantum simulations is shown to improve estimation of local observables relative to unencoded runs. Together, the developments in this thesis mark practical progress toward fault-tolerant quantum simulations of fundamental physics capable of scientific discovery.

item.title: Nonorthogonal variational quantum simulation for quantum chemistry
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Linear combinations of nonorthogonal parameterized quantum circuits achieve dynamic state simulation and imaginary-time ground states using shallow or single-layer circuits, reaching sub-chemical accuracy with 18 single-layer circuits for N2 ($6e, 6o$).

Grade 0.412 · 2.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Probing many-body dynamics on a 51-atom quantum simulator” · Zongkang Zhang, Jiajun Ren, Xiao Yuan

Figure

Energy of the 12-qubit N2 molecule plotted against interatomic distance. 18 single-layer PQCs evolved in imaginary time match exact imaginary-time evolution and FCI across equilibrium and dissociation regimes.

Asks

How can nonorthogonal multi-state ansatzes be extended to variational quantum simulation to enhance wavefunction expressivity under strict circuit-depth limits?

Before

Conventional VQS using a single deep parameterized quantum circuit, which requires significantly deeper circuits to match expressivity.

But

Classical shadow measurement circuit overhead grows from 𝒪(NpNd) to 𝒪(NpNd+Nc); accuracy depends on initial reference state overlap, deteriorating in multireference dissociation regimes.

Tools

nonorthogonal variational quantum simulation (NOVQS) · McLachlan's variational principle · fermionic simulation (fSim) gates · classical shadows · ancilla-free Hadamard tests

Abstract

Dynamical simulation of quantum many-body systems is a central task in quantum chemistry and requires efficient wavefunction representations. Although tensor-network and neural-network quantum states have achieved considerable success in ground-state calculations, entanglement growth hinders their application to quantum dynamics. Quantum computing may offer a route to quantum advantage, but algorithms such as Trotterization generally require fault-tolerant quantum computers, whereas near-term hardware supports only limited circuit sizes. Variational quantum simulation (VQS) instead represents the evolving state with a single shallow, fixed-size parameterized quantum circuit (PQC). Here, we introduce nonorthogonal variational quantum simulation (NOVQS), which applies linear combinations of parameterized quantum states to real- and imaginary-time evolutions. We design a shallow, hardware-friendly ansatz tailored to second-quantized electronic-structure Hamiltonians, together with resource-efficient protocols for measuring the matrices and vectors in the parameter equations of motion. Error analysis and resource estimation are also provided. Numerical simulations of hydrogen chains and the nitrogen molecule demonstrate that a collection of shallow, or even single-layer, PQCs can match or outperform a much deeper PQC in VQS. In particular, we identify a trade-off between circuit number and depth. NOVQS therefore provides a flexible route to enhancing wavefunction expressivity under circuit-depth constraints, making it a promising framework for quantum dynamics simulations on near-term quantum processors.

item.title: On the numerical limitations of dual Koopman von Neumann embeddings for solving conservative nonlinear ordinary differential equations on quantum computers
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Trajectories of conservative nonlinear ODEs reconstructed via quantum simulation of dual Koopman–von Neumann Liouville densities incur an Ehrenfest reconstruction error bounded by density covariance and flow Hessian, scaling with measurement cost O(1/ϵ) via amplitude estimation.

Grade 0.376 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Probing many-body dynamics on a 51-atom quantum simulator” · Thibault Fredon, Abhay K. Ram, Fabrice Debbasch, Julien Zylberman, Nuno F. Loureiro

Figure

Error between the reference RK4 trajectory and the reconstructed Liouville mean over time alongside theoretical bounds and covariance growth for the quartic oscillator.

Asks

What are the computational and accuracy limits when solving nonlinear ordinary differential equations on quantum computers using dual Koopman–von Neumann Liouville density embeddings?

But

Conservative or measure-preserving autonomous systems with divergence-free vector fields; trade-off requiring narrow initial Gaussian widths that remain resolved on a 2n×d grid without under-resolution artifacts.

Tools

Koopman–von Neumann (KvN) formalism · Liouville transport equation simulation · Hadamard test and Grover-type amplitude estimation · Ehrenfest error analysis

Abstract

The simulation of nonlinear ordinary differential equations on quantum computers is inherently challenging, as quantum gates are linear operators on qubit states. In this paper, we put forth a Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) operator based algorithm for solving nonlinear ordinary differential equations on a quantum computer which overcomes the innate limitations of quantum operations. In this approach, a Liouville probability density is embedded into a wavefunction, the evolution of which is governed by an operator dual to the Koopman operator. The trajectories corresponding to the nonlinear differential equations are reconstructed from the average value of Koopman observables evaluated through quantum measurements. We specifically evaluate the computational limitations of solving nonlinear equations within this Liouville embedding framework. An Ehrenfest-type estimate is derived that relates the reconstruction error to the covariance of the transported density, highlighting the competition between linear stretching and Hessian-induced folding.This leads to a key stability criterion, which depends on the local Ehrenfest-Reynolds number. We discuss the effects of measurement-induced errors including those due to Hadamard-test sampling, amplitude estimation, and bias due to covariance in probabilistic Grover-type inference on the evaluation of trajectories. The limiting bounds on the accuracy of quantum computations are numerically verified for the Lotka-Volterra system and for the quartic oscillator. We observe a rapid growth in computational errors when the Ehrenfest-Reynolds number approaches the predicted threshold. The bounds resulting from our analysis provide key guidelines for selecting the width of the initial Gaussian probability distribution associated with a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations.

item.title: Evaluation-efficient quantum architecture search with ZX-calculus-based topological reuse
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Combining ternary Gray-code search-space mapping with ZX-calculus topological similarity reuse achieves an evaluation reuse rate of 45.75% (evaluation cost savings exceeding 40%) while preserving ground-state convergence under noise.

Grade 0.353 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “quantum chemistry and electronic structure on quantum computers” · Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, Dazhi Ding

Figure

Evaluation frequency per generation across the 1D transverse-field Ising model search. Green bars show evaluated new topologies and light-blue bars show redundant topologies bypassed by ZX reuse, showing evaluations dropping from ~20 to 2–4 per generation as the search converges.

Asks

How to reduce expensive candidate circuit evaluations in quantum architecture search under noisy intermediate-scale quantum conditions without degrading convergence?

But

Evaluated on molecular ground-state simulations (H2, LiH, H4) and 1D transverse-field Ising model; introduces potential approximation error requiring task-specific tuning of similarity threshold, reuse penalty, and minimum real-evaluation probability.

Tools

ZX-calculus graph simplification · Ternary Gray-code mapping · Noise-aware parameter-sharing supernet · Evolutionary algorithm

Abstract

Variational quantum algorithm is a leading approach for quantum chemistry and many-body physics on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. The performance depends strongly on the structure of the parameterized quantum circuits. Quantum architecture search (QAS) can automate ansatz design. However, it requires repeated training and evaluation of many candidate circuits, leading to high evaluation cost. In this work, we propose a noise-aware quantum architecture search framework based on ZX-calculus topological reuse (ZX-QAS). The framework encodes the search space with a ternary Gray-code mapping and integrates a noise-aware quantum neural network with a ZX-calculus topological reuse mechanism. The effectiveness of the framework is validated through ground-state energy estimation tasks and one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model tasks under noisy conditions. The results show that the ZX-QAS exhibits stable convergence and remarkably reduces the cost of expensive evaluations under noisy conditions.

item.title: Avoided crossings in spin-boson systems: consequences for adiabatic state preparation
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Avoided crossings and reduced energy gaps constrain adiabatic switching times for correlated state preparation in finite spin-boson models. Preparing local Pauli observables requires non-monotonic switching times with an anomalous peak at γ≈3.3, driven by persistent coherent oscillations across narrow gaps.

Grade 0.348 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Probing many-body dynamics on a 51-atom quantum simulator” · Joona Marjamäki, Robert van Leeuwen, Riku Tuovinen

Figure

Switch-on time t0 and oscillation amplitude vs effective coupling strength γ for Pauli observables ⟨σz⟩ and ⟨σx⟩. Shows non-monotonic preparation times peaking near resonance γ≈3.3 due to persistent coherent oscillations across narrow avoided-crossing gaps.

Asks

How do avoided crossings in the correlated many-body spectrum limit the efficiency and switching times of adiabatic state preparation in finite spin-boson systems?

But

Restricted to finite discrete bosonic baths (1 and 3 modes), zero temperature, and truncated Hilbert spaces converged within a 10−6 energy tolerance.

Tools

Exact diagonalization · Time-dependent adiabatic switching · Lorentz-Drude spectral function · Truncated bosonic Hilbert space

Abstract

Avoided crossings in the correlated many-body spectrum play a central role in determining the conditions for adiabatic state preparation in interacting quantum systems. We investigate this connection in finite spin-boson systems by combining exact diagonalization of the many-body spectrum with time-dependent simulations of adiabatic switching protocols. By comparing the adiabatically prepared state with the exact ground state, we determine the switching times required for reliable preparation as a function of the spin-boson coupling strength and bosonic mode structure. We show that regions of small many-body level spacings, associated with avoided crossings, impose the strongest constraints on adiabatic preparation and explain the observed dependence of the required switching times on the interaction strength. Furthermore, while the ground-state energy follows the overall spectral trends, local observables such as Pauli matrix expectation values exhibit additional non-monotonic behavior arising from coherent oscillations in finite systems. These findings can provide concrete benchmarks for both the theoretical treatment of open quantum systems and practical implementations in quantum simulation and qubit control.

item.title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Quantum Trajectories
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Stochastic time-dependent variational principle combined with multi-Gaussian wavepacket superposition (sVMG) simulates open bosonic quantum trajectories analytically, reproducing exact non-Gaussian trajectories and bipartite entanglement on a dimer while demonstrating a 2D checkerboard symmetry-breaking transition that vanishes in 1D chains.

Grade 0.343 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum simulations with ultracold quantum gases” · Zejian Li, Jacopo Tosca

Figure

Steady-state normalized π-mode population ⟨nˆπ⟩/N versus coherent drive F/γ across multiple lattice sizes N. The 1D chain order parameter decays to zero with increasing N, whereas the 2D lattice retains a finite dome-shaped profile indicating a symmetry-broken phase.

Asks

How can stochastic quantum trajectory dynamics and non-Gaussian correlations in interacting open bosonic systems be efficiently simulated beyond semiclassical approximations?

Before

Truncated Wigner approximation and Gaussian trajectory approximations fail to capture single-trajectory non-Gaussian dynamics and entanglement entropy.

But

Applied to driven-dissipative Bose-Hubbard models under heterodyne quantum state diffusion unraveling with single-body loss; uses low-rank covariance decomposition with rank K=2 and Nc=4 components for larger lattices.

Tools

stochastic time-dependent variational principle (sTDVP) · Stratonovich stochastic Schrödinger equation · multi-Gaussian wavefunction ansatz · Euler-Heun numerical integration · Tikhonov regularization

Abstract

We propose a variational framework for the efficient simulation of stochastic quantum dynamics in interacting bosonic systems. Our method generalizes the time-dependent variational principle to accommodate quantum state diffusion processes and is tailored for describing quantum trajectories unraveled from a master equation. We adopt a wavefunction ansatz composed of a coherent superposition of Gaussian wavepackets, which allows the fully analytical assembly of the variational equations of motion while capturing both the quantum trajectory dynamics and the Lindblad evolution beyond semiclassical approximations. The method is carefully benchmarked on a Bose-Hubbard dimer, and applied to extended Bose-Hubbard lattices in both 1D and 2D. In particular, we show the emergence of a symmetry-breaking phase transition in 2D lattices, which is absent in 1D chains.
